display.title: Episode 345: The Storyteller, Chapter 8 (Erev Yom Kippur)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Erev Yom Kippur show: what Tashlich teaches about teshuvah, Shema with a second-grade class, the Baal Shem Tov reveals a young man's Jewish roots, and the laws of the fast.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Erev Yom Kippur 5749. Uncle Yossi explains why we say Tashlich by flowing water: something thrown into a moving river is carried away for good, just as true teshuvah means never taking the sins back. The mitzvah of the day is teshuvah, to daven, say brachos and give tzedakah better than before, along with the Rebbe's call to start the year with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah, all with simcha. After the Hakochainik march and a word from the sponsor, story time continues 'The Storyteller': the Baal Shem Tov tells Alex that he is really Yitzchak, a Jewish child saved from a fire and raised in an orphanage, and welcomes him back to his people. A second-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school leads the Shema. The story resumes as Yitzchak promises to follow the Baal Shem Tov and asks for a sign that his teshuvah has been accepted, and the chapter stops just as the sign is about to be revealed. Uncle Yossi closes with the seudah of Erev Yom Kippur, the laws of the fast, the yahrzeit lamp, and the Shema and shofar at the end of Neilah.
display.lesson: Teshuvah means truly leaving our mistakes behind, like throwing them into a flowing river, and it is never too late to return to Hashem.
